note: PROBE BUG, not a port bug. The 7e-4 FEED drift (js=0.01353 cs=0.01352) traced to its source: tools/_probe_damage.mjs's FEED/BRIDGE/JOIN sections built their own local stand-in cartridges (pistolCart={bullet:9.02,energy:580}, akmCart={bullet:7.92,energy:2000}, bellyCart={bullet:12.7,energy:16000}) instead of importing the real CARTRIDGES table from src/ballistics.js:78-133. DamageProbe.cs's FeedGrowthFacts()/BridgeAndJoinFacts() correctly read Cartridges.Para9x19/M43_762x39/Heavy127x108 from the REAL ported Combat/Ballistics.cs (bullet 9.01/7.92/12.98 mm, energy 580.6/2019.3/16238.5 J — derived via 0.5*m*v0^2, not literals). So the two sides disagreed on INPUT (9.02mm vs the real 9.01mm bullet diameter), not on arithmetic: tearRadius(cal,1)=1.5*cal amplified the 0.01mm input difference into the 7e-4 relative drift on r. None of the three float-precision causes named in the unity skill (fract-hash double, accumulator, Mathf.RoundToInt-vs-Math.round) applied — ruled out by tracing cal/r by hand on both sides before touching any code. Fix: tools/_probe_damage.mjs now imports { CARTRIDGES } from '../src/ballistics.js' and uses CARTRIDGES['9x19']/['7.62x39']/['12.7x108'] in place of the three stand-in literals (both the FEED block and the BRIDGE/JOIN loop). This also silently fixed BRIDGE/JOIN's own pre-existing input mismatch (belly bulletMm 12.7 vs the real 12.98 was the worst, rel=2.16e-2) which the 12-mismatch display cap in tools/unity_port_check.py had been hiding behind the FEED failures. After the fix: FEED and BRIDGE/JOIN lines match CS to float32 precision (0 relative difference at the printed precision). Residual, OUT-OF-SCOPE float noise still present in the same probe pair (TEARRADIUS id=762x39_n2/127x108_n2, ~3-5e-5 relative, just over the 1e-5 tolerance, likely Mathf.Pow(1f,0.6f) vs Math.pow(1,0.6) base-1 special-casing; GLASS id=shatter steps=50 vs 49, an off-by-one rest-frame threshold crossing; BREAKWALL id=crumble 3.3e-4) was NOT touched — it predates this fix, was masked by the same 12-entry cap, and is unrelated to the FEED/cartridge bug this task scoped. Flagging it as an honest open item rather than silently leaving it.

PROBE BUG, not a port bug (and the real numbers were already verified; only the probe's VERDICT was wrong). tools/_probe_crashmath.mjs prints 26 lines: 8 CRASHM lines (5 cross + 3 reflect, mback_*/side_* or r_*) that DO have a CrashProbe.cs counterpart, and 18 CRASHM_CHECK lines (3 per cross id x5 + 1 per reflect id x3: handWrittenIsCross/swapMatches/unswappedIsNegative/mirrorInvariant) that are the JS script's OWN self-verification of its hand-written formula — proving src/crash.js:130's `new THREE.Vector3(-back.z,0,back.x)` really is algebraically back.cross(up), using THREE's own cross()/reflect(), with no Unity involved. These 18 lines lacked the tools/unity_port_check.py JSONLY prefix convention (its one_sided() check), so every one counted as an unmatched js-only line and pushed the probe to FAIL (12 shown, all 'no C# line matching') even though the 8 real CRASHM pairs (39 values) matched CS to 0.000e+00 relative difference, both before and after this fix — the FEED-style numeric drift never existed here. Investigated whether the 3-line shape belongs on the C# side (the task's stated preference) and found a concrete reason it cannot be: Core/CrashSequence.cs:194 calls `Vector3.Cross(Vector3.up, back)` directly and carries no second, independently hand-written cross formula to re-derive against — porting 'handWrittenIsCross' etc. to C# would mean inventing a redundant hand-rolled cross just to prove it equals Vector3.Cross, testing the test rather than the port. Fixed on the JS side instead: the check() helper now prints `JSONLY CRASHM_CHECK ...` (one line changed, tools/_probe_crashmath.mjs's check() function), which tools/unity_port_check.py already treats as a by-design one-sided fact (counted, never paired, no longer a failure). Verified: `python3 tools/unity_port_check.py` now reports 'compared 39 values across 8 js / 8 cs lines ... one-sided facts not paired (by design): 18 js, 0 cs ... PASS - 39 values match to float32 precision' (was FAIL before, same 39/39 match underneath).
